sample_unit: cases (development cohort: 7825 mediastinal neoplasm cases plus 796 normal controls)

links.outcome: Clinician top-1 and top-3 diagnostic accuracy with versus without CAIMEN-based software assistance
links.effect: 46 clinicians improved average top-1 accuracy by 19.1% and top-3 accuracy by 13.0% with AI assistance; CAIMEN alone also outperformed clinicians (top-1 0.500, top-3 0.800).
links.quote: with assistance from the computer aided diagnosis software based on CAIMEN, the 46 clinicians improved their average top-1 accuracy by 19·1% (0·345-0·411) and top-3 accuracy by 13·0% (0·545-0·616).

unlisted_practices: federated learning across 24 centres for privacy-preserving model development

screen.reason: The study conducts a human-AI experiment with 46 clinicians comparing diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance.

primary.practice: AI assistance in clinician diagnostic workflow
